newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends weaker in thin hedge selling.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends weaker in thin hedge selling.

text.p: MGE spring wheat settled weaker on Friday in thin dealings on some hedge-type selling.
"The biggest problem is the lack of volume. We did see some commercial hedge pressure," a trader said.
"Export news was very light. There may be some Pakistan export business that is supposed to show up over the weekend but that would be optional origin," the trader added.

Atwood bought 600,000 bushels March wheat and sold 400,000 March wheat. Benson Quinn bought 400,000 March and sold 700,000 March and Country Hedging bought 100,000 March and sold 800,000 March wheat, the trader said.

CIS bought 300,000 bushels of March wheat, Wilson Trading purchased 800,000 March, bought 200,000 May and sold 400,000 July. A big player was LFG which bought 1.2 million bushels March wheat, 700,000 May, 400,000 July and 400,000 September wheat. LFG sold 200,000 bushels of March wheat, he said.
MGE spring wheat was 3-3/4 to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower with March down 4-1/4 cents at $3.92-1/2.
